name: Primary Thyroid Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunophenotypic Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Thyroid Lymphoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of lymphoma involving the thyroid gland with characteristic lymphoid infiltration
Immunohistochemical evidence of B-cell markers (e.g., CD20 positivity) consistent with lymphoma subtype
Imaging studies showing a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass without distant nodal involvement at presentation
Exclusion of systemic lymphoma or secondary thyroid involvement by lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of lymphoma in the thyroid with immunophenotypic evidence and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Fine needle aspiration biopsy may be insufficient; core biopsy or surgical biopsy often required for definitive diagnosis.

searchTerms: difficulty breathing through nose or throat

laboratory: Thyroid function tests may show hypothyroidism
imaging: Ultrasound showing hypoechoic, heterogeneous thyroid mass
CT/MRI demonstrating thyroid enlargement with local invasion
PET scan showing increased FDG uptake localized to thyroid
genetic: Clonal rearrangement of immunoglobulin heavy chain genes
Chromosomal abnormalities such as t(11;18)(q21;q21) in MALT lymphoma subtype
other: Histopathology revealing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma or MALT lymphoma subtype

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epithelial markers on immunohistochemistry
Rapidly enlarging mass with necrosis and hemorrhage
Diffuse thyroid enlargement without discrete mass

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging thyroid mass over weeks
Unexplained B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
references: Cibas ES, Ducatman BS. Cytology: Diagnostic Principles and Clinical Correlates. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2014.
Thyroid lymphoma: clinical features, diagnosis, and management. UpToDate. 2024.
Orphanet: Primary thyroid lymphoma. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
